sources.title: Tomasz Kochanek, Functional Analysis, Lecture 1: Normed space; examples; Riesz' lemma; equivalence of norms
sources.locator: PDF p. 1, Definition 1.1 and the induced norm metric; the complete five-page lecture was inspected.
sources.reading_verification: Inspected all five pages of the locally retained extracted text at research/quantum-build-60-2026-10-15-owner/norms/sources/lecture1.txt and the corresponding PDF. Definition 1.1 treats norms over K=R or C and gives the induced norm metric. The source supports the norm/metric conventions; the subspace restriction and basis conversion are proved locally.

contents.name: Norms over either scalar field and the induced norm metric
contents.locator: PDF p. 1, Definition 1.1 and the following metric paragraph
contents.support: The notes define the norm axioms for K equal to R or C and associate the metric rho(x,y)=||x-y||. They do not supply the subspace realification or finite-basis argument, which is written out locally.

sources.title: M. S. Moslehian, G. A. Muñoz-Fernández, A. M. Peralta, and J. B. Seoane-Sepúlveda, Similarities and differences between real and complex Banach spaces: an overview and recent developments
sources.locator: Section 2.1, Linear algebra, PDF p. 5 (journal p. 88); article metadata inspected on PDF p. 1.
sources.reading_verification: Inspected the full-text 80-page PDF's title/authors/publication data and the complete Section 2 Real vs complex linear spaces, especially Section 2.1. It states scalar restriction as realification and the finite basis f1,if1,...,fn,ifn. The local proof supplies the subspace norm/metric restriction and independently proves spanning, independence, injectivity, and n=0.

contents.name: Realification and the real basis induced by a finite complex basis
contents.locator: Section 2.1, Linear algebra, PDF p. 5 (journal p. 88)
contents.support: The article states that restriction of scalars makes a complex linear space a real linear space and that a finite complex basis f1,...,fn gives the real basis f1,if1,...,fn,ifn. The local proof checks the exact supplied-list and zero-dimensional cases and adds the normed-subspace metric conclusion.
